resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (Resale/Rental and UFSA inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Carneys Point Township Housing Office (Office of Housing and Inspection)
resale_co.lead_time: Submit the Certificate of Occupancy application at least 3 weeks before settlement. Inspections must be scheduled by 3 p.m. and at least 48 hours ahead.
requirements: Buyer may not occupy the home until the Township issues a certificate of occupancy (Township code section 64-2)
All construction permits must be in place for anything newly or previously installed or replaced, such as air conditioning/HVAC, water heater, furnace or chimney
Well, chimney and septic certifications are required when the property has them
Inspector may cite any other item under the International Property Maintenance Code
Smoke, carbon monoxide and secondary power source label inspection (UFSA) is done by the same office on the same application

fees.label: Residential resale inspection, initial inspection and one re-inspection
fees.quote: RESIDENTIAL RE-SALES: (1) $125.00- for the initial inspection and one re-inspection

fees.label: Resale/rental application fee, total of certificate of occupancy fee and fire (smoke/carbon monoxide) inspection when not a rush
fees.quote: Resale/Rental Application Fee $170 (C/O Fee $125 & Fire Inspection $45 if not a rush inspection)

fees.label: Returned check
fees.quote: PLEASE NOTE: A $20 fee will be assessed for any returned checked!

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township's Resale/Rental and UFSA Application (check 'Resale/UFSA'), listing the property, owner, buyer, both agents and any well, chimney or septic, and submit it to the Housing Office at 303 Harding Highway with payment at least 3 weeks before settlement. Payment must be exact cash, check or money order made out to Carneys Point Twp and is due with the application before review or scheduling. When emailing the Housing and Zoning Department, put the address or block and lot in the subject line.
resale_co.contact_title: Housing / Zoning / Public Health Officer / Vacant Property

evidence.quote: nor shall any person, group of persons, association, partnership or corporation, or any combination thereof, purchasing or acquiring, in any manner, occupy a dwelling unit or permit it to be occupied by another without first securing from the Office of Housing and Inspection of the Township a certificate of occupancy for said dwelling unit.
Please Note: Certificate of Occupancy Applications must be submitted at least 3 weeks prior to the date of settlement or rental occupancy.
All C/O Inspections must be scheduled by 3pm and at least 48 hours prior to the date of inspection.
Housing / Zoning / Public Health Officer/vacant propertyRobert Schmid 856-299-0070 x128 housingzoningofficer@carneyspointtwp.org
Payments are accepted via EXACT cash, check, or money order. This must be submitted with all applications prior to review and/or scheduling

Prior to inspections, please ensure that ALL of the proper construction permits have been obtained for any and ALL structures that have been newly or previously installed or replaced (Examples are: AC/HVAC systems, water heaters, furnace, chimney etc.)

resale_co.notes: Carneys Point runs one combined Resale/Rental and UFSA (Uniform Fire Safety Act) inspection through its Housing Office: the certificate of occupancy and the smoke/carbon monoxide certificate are applied for on the same form. The Housing Assistant, Demi Romansky (856-299-0070 x127, housingassistant@carneyspointtwp.org, Monday to Friday 8:00am to 3:30pm), handles the office; Robert Schmid's inspection hours are Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday 12:30pm to 2:30pm and office hours 2:30pm to 3:30pm. The Housing page also lists a $25 Zoning Application Fee; it is not clear whether a zoning application is needed for a resale. The Township code is on ecode360 (CA0753) and could not be opened; the ordinance text quoted comes from the Township's own application form. No validity period is stated.

requirements: 10-year sealed smoke detectors in the common area and in each separate sleeping room
10-year sealed smoke detector within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
10-year sealed smoke detector on each additional story, including the basement (not crawl spaces or uninhabitable attics)
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of each bedroom in homes with fuel burning appliances or an attached garage
Homes with a secondary power source need a warning label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter
Newly built or renovated homes must have hardwired, interconnected smoke and carbon monoxide detectors with battery backup; regular battery-only detectors are no longer allowed

fire_cert.notes: The State (NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety) is the fire code enforcing agency for Carneys Point (registry code S; state directory code 1713), but the State does not issue the smoke certificate here: the DCA state towns list (revised 7/17/2026) shows Carneys Point without the 'SC' mark, and the DCA portal data marks CARNEYS POINT TWP-001 as smoke-certificate exempt. The Township's Housing Office does the smoke, carbon monoxide and power source label inspection itself on its combined Resale/UFSA application. The state fire directory still lists 'NJ Division Fire Safety' under smoke detector compliance; the Township's own 2026 forms are used here. The Township checklist lists no fire extinguisher, in line with P.L.2025, c.19. The Carneys Point Fire & Rescue chief (Ted Stranahan) runs the volunteer fire company, not the inspection.
